name: On/off-chain interaction
definition: Design patterns whose components sit both off-chain and on-chain. They bridge off-chain systems with on-chain data or smart contracts. This category is central to dApp design because a blockchain cannot natively request external data.

name: On-chain - Domain-based
definition: On-chain patterns that implement domain features (BPM, identity, big data, and features reusable across domains). The SLR treats this as an intermediate category under On-chain pattern, intended to grow as new domain-specific patterns appear.

name: On-chain - Smart contract
definition: Patterns about implementing and managing smart contracts: how contracts are organized together, secured, made cheaper to execute, and how function access is authorized.

name: On-chain - Data management
definition: Patterns for efficient management of data that already live on-chain, in smart contracts or transactions. Distinct from the On/off-chain 'Data management' subcategory, which keeps the payload off-chain and only uses the chain for integrity or trust.

name: Architectural
definition: Architectural patterns about who creates and signs blockchain transactions (user, browser wallet confirmation, or a delegated service). The SLR places them outside the design-pattern taxonomy proper because only three were found; this working catalog keeps them as a first-class category.

name: Idiom
definition: Solidity idioms that reduce execution fees by packing storage, choosing integer/mapping layouts, or freeing unused slots. The SLR found no dedicated idiom papers but classified 14 such items separately from design patterns; this catalog keeps them as a category.

name: Data exchange
definition: Patterns that enable communication between on-chain smart contracts and off-chain components. Blockchain cannot pull external data, so an external service (e.g. an Oracle) must push fresh data into contracts.

name: Data management
definition: Patterns that keep data off-chain but use the blockchain to guarantee tamper-proofing or trustability (e.g. hashing a dataset and storing the hash on-chain). Not the same as on-chain Data management.

name: Wallet and keys
definition: Patterns for managing wallets and cryptographic keys in a decentralized application.

name: Transactions
definition: Patterns about transaction aspects between off-chain components and the blockchain, such as confirmation or block inclusion.

name: BPM
definition: On-chain business process management: encoding activities, engines, or choreography so collaborative processes run with blockchain as software connector.

name: Decentralized identity
definition: Patterns that use blockchain to create and manage decentralized identities.

name: Big data
definition: Applications of blockchain to big data, such as registering operations performed on a data store.

name: Multi-domain feature
definition: On-chain features that do not belong to one particular domain but can be reused across domains (voting, randomness, access windows, reputation, state machines, etc.).

name: Contract management
definition: Patterns for organizing smart contracts together, for example a proxy that relays calls to an implementation that can be replaced.

name: Contract security
definition: Smart-contract security patterns addressing issues such as reentrancy, overflow, or flawed contract behavior.

name: Contract efficiency
definition: Patterns that reduce the cost of using smart contracts, especially on public chains, including data-refresh problems because contracts cannot request other contracts by themselves.

name: Contract access control
definition: Patterns for permission and authorization over the execution of smart-contract functions.

name: Storage
definition: Patterns that deal with how data are stored on-chain (immutability, append-only logs, packing, separating data from logic).

name: Encryption
definition: Patterns for on-chain data encryption or delayed disclosure, including commit-reveal and zero-knowledge verification.

name: Migration
definition: Patterns that help migrate data, state, or contracts from one blockchain to another (snapshotting, genesis, translation).

name: Tokenization
definition: Represent an asset as an on-chain token (fungible or NFT) so it can be issued, transferred, and tracked through standard interfaces.
